objectives: To determine the frequency and characteristics of genitourinary manifestations in patients with long COVID and to evaluate the evidence supporting the possible emergence of a genitourinary phenotype within long COVID.
inclusion_criteria: Primary observational studies (cross-sectional, cohort, and case-control) evaluating individuals of any age with one or more genitourinary symptoms in the context of long COVID were included. Eligible symptoms included decline in renal function, urinary incontinence, urgency, frequency, voiding dysfunction, erectile dysfunction, scrotal pain, epididymo-orchitis, and menstrual alterations. Long COVID was defined as persistence or recurrence of symptoms >=12 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection confirmed by PCR, antigen testing, or clinical criteria. No restrictions were applied regarding language, publication year, or publication status.
exclusion_criteria: Studies were excluded if they included only individuals without genitourinary manifestations, focused only on acute-phase manifestations or disease duration <12 weeks, did not specify timing of symptom onset in relation to SARS-CoV-2 infection, addressed vaccine-related effects, or involved pre-existing genitourinary conditions/disorders unrelated to COVID-19. Letters to the editor, commentaries, editorials, narrative reviews, posters, and other manuscripts without original data were also excluded.
